newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria mulls pegging lev to German mark.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria mulls pegging lev to German mark.

text.p: Bulgaria's Financial Stabilisation Council has proposed pegging the lev to the mark in a fixed exchange rate regime aimed at restoring confidence in the national currency, officials said on Monday.

"We will propose to the cabinet and parliament our draft, which envisages the German mark as an anchor currency in the future currency board mechanism," Economic Policy Minister Krassimir Angarski told Reuters.
Arguments supporting the mark prevailed over the U.S. dollar at the council's meeting last week, he added.

Traditionally the dollar has been perceived as a benchmark of stability as people convert their savings mostly into dollars. The bulk of Bulgaria's $9.6 billion foreign debt is also mostly in dollars.

"Bulgaria needs to adjust to a new economic cycle compatible with its geopolitical and economic ties. Linking the lev to the mark has many advantages for the country's future as it aspires to a full European Union membership," Bulbank executive director Chavdar Kanchev told Reuters.
Germany is Bulgaria's biggest trade partner and investor.

Lower international interest rates for the mark compared to the rates for the dollar would also help reduce the current wide margin between lev interest rates and hard currency rates, said Kanchev, who is also a member of the council.

Under a $548 million 14-month standby agreement sealed with the IMF last month, Bulgaria pledged to introduce a self-regulating restrictive monetary mechanism, known as a currency board, in a bid to stabilise its shaky financial system.

Under the currency board system the lev will be pegged to an anchor currency, at a rate that cannot be adjusted. The amount of levs in circulation must be matched precisely by the amount of foreign exchange reserves.
An International Monetary Fund (IMF) technical mission arrived on Monday to help draft necessary legal amendments needed to make the board operational.

The new cabinet, due to be formed by May 20 by the reformist Union of Democratic Forces, the winner in April 19 general elections, is expected to consider the amendments jointly with the IMF and introduce them to parliament.
The currency board system is expected to be introduced in July, said Angarski. The system bans the central bank from lending to commercial banks and the government.

The IMF has said that the lev would be pegged at about the market rate at the time of introduction. The lev has stabilised since its collapse early this year to trade at about 1,500 to the dollar. The daily central bank fixing for Monday was 865.68 levs to the mark. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-981-4145
